items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s become an elitist — it’s become elite. A lot of people don’t really understand it you know. It’s a passing fad or diversion. But well it’s like what classical music became, and then classical music had problems, it became the same way. Even like in the, you

know like Ludwig in Bavaria. You’d have a composer write a tune and just his friends come to hear it. They’d sit there in a two thousand seat theater with about twenty people, his cronies would listen to it. The people couldn’t hear it. I don’t mean to call names, but this is what royalty did. They would give chamber music, and I guess that’s where “chamber” the term came from.
